data.body:
Caller-dependency gate + decision checkpoint. Serena and string-reference sweeps found two production `pending_enrichment` consumers: `drain()` needs the complete sorted candidates for batch/claim processing (`enrich_drain.py:204-230`); `maybe_drain()` only needs a boolean (`:313-326`) and is reached after durable push from both write paths. Expected repair contract: <=20 ms caller gate, identical soak/latest-enqueue/done/lease/claim eligibility, complete drain candidates, no missed enqueue.

Behavior-equivalent stateless probes cannot meet that contract: one shared directory scan preserved all 4,371 states but averaged 224 ms; identity+scandir preserved all states but averaged 310 ms; Git tracked-path enumeration alone costs 12-16 ms, and an exact Git-index candidate reducer preserved all 771 queue-ticket states but averaged 69.5 ms. No caller depends on slowness, but callers do depend on exact eligibility/list semantics.

Therefore repair now requires operator-approved design/behavior: (A, recommended) move the exact scan off the caller into a detached coalesced gate/drain child, preserving the event log and reducer but allowing a child launch when no item qualifies; (B) add a persistent derived HEAD-keyed queue-state index with explicit atomicity/invalidation/rebuild policy; (C) accept ~70 ms and raise the 20 ms budget; or (D) disable/scope opportunistic drain. A avoids a second consistency model but needs a bounded-spawn/lock-coalescing contract and changes when the eligibility check executes. Per directive, implementation stops here pending operator review. No production/test edits or plan review have begun.
